newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rebels put troops to flight in south.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebels put troops to flight in south.

text.p: Rebels in this main southern Albanian town put newly-arrived government troops to flight on Saturday and arrested their one-star general, eyewitnesses and diplomats told Reuters.

Dozens of troops, who had just arrived by helicopter to bolster morale in the main government stronghold in the south, ran off into the surrounding forests and hills after being confronted by rebels and angry residents, the eyewitnesses said.

"Gjirokaster is now under the control of the rebels," a diplomat who requested anonymity said. About 30 km (20 miles) from the Greek border, Gjirokaster was the last main government stronghold in southern Albania.
Eyewitnesses said most of the troops, who arrived in about six helicopters on Saturday, had retreated in disarray and were held up in the Ayia Triada monastery, two km (one mile) east of the town.
In what appeared to be a humiliating defeat for President Sali Berisha, the other soldiers, a company of at least 120 men, were fleeing into the woods.
